# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1558 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1558 - **Title**: gh-1555 [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1555` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 11 - **Additions**: +586 - **Deletions**: -23 - **Created**: 2026-10-11T21:05:18Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T22:02:58Z ## PR Description Closes #1555 ## gh-1555 W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (first shippable slice) ### What changed Migrated the legacy full-open call sites (ticket mechanism d1–d7) to windowed opens so a session past the 2 GiB gh-1073 backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path. The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). Known pre-existing, reproduced on unmodified main: `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts the VM at teardown (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`) and kills whole-directory `dart test` runs that include it — run it in isolation.
Architecture diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph before [before W1] P1[Picker / resume / trajectory / child preview] --> F[repo.open full] F -->|> 2 GiB| X[SessionException tooLarge] end subgraph after [after W1] P2[Picker · /resume · name scan · child preview] --> W[repo.open windowed] T[fa trajectory view/cost/inspect] --> W W --> H[ensureWholeLedgerResident
loadAllOlder: bounded blocks, one splice] W --> N[resolveSessionName
paged name lookup] TL[fa trajectory tail] --> W end ```

- Both offenders are methods **introduced by this PR** (the ratchet is whole-repo, threshold pinned at 12.0 in `crap4dart.yaml`; at 100% coverage CRAP equals cyclomatic complexity, so CC ≤ 12 is the hard rule):

  - `resolveTrajectorySession` (trajectory_tui.dart) — CC 13, 100% coverage → CRAP 13.00
- No open PR review threads (0 at rework start), no merge conflicts.

## Approach

Followed the repo's established ratchet pattern (same one the config comment documents for the CC-12 trio: "split into cohesive sub-dispatchers"). Pure behavior-preserving extractions — no logic changed:

1. **`WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder`** split into three cohesive members:

   - `_isScanSkippable(entry, top)` — the three skip classes (header line, at/above window top, already-indexed straddler); CC 3.
   - `_spliceOlderAbove(records, starts, ends)` — the single-prepend splice + re-index; CC 2.
   - `loadAllOlder` keeps only the guard and orchestration; CC 14 → 4.
2. **`resolveTrajectorySession`** — the two name-match loops (foreign-repo windowed scan + `JsonlSessionRepo.sessionNameQuick`) extracted into `_openTrajectoryByName(repo, sessions, wanted)`; resolver CC 13 → 6, helper CC 8.

- Both offenders are methods **introduced by this PR** (the ratchet is whole-repo, threshold pinned at 12.0 in `crap4dart.yaml`; at 100% coverage CRAP equals cyclomatic complexity, so CC ≤ 12 is the hard rule):

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1558 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1558 - **Title**: gh-1555 [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1555` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 11 - **Additions**: +586 - **Deletions**: -23 - **Created**: 2026-10-11T21:05:18Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T22:02:58Z ## PR Description Closes #1555 ## gh-1555 W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (first shippable slice) ### What changed Migrated the legacy full-open call sites (ticket mechanism d1–d7) to windowed opens so a session past the 2 GiB gh-1073 backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path. The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). Known pre-existing, reproduced on unmodified main: `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts the VM at teardown (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`) and kills whole-directory `dart test` runs that include it — run it in isolation.

loadAllOlder: bounded blocks, one splice] W --> N[resolveSessionName
paged name lookup] TL[fa trajectory tail] --> W end ```

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1558 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1558 - **Title**: gh-1555 [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1555` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 11 - **Additions**: +586 - **Deletions**: -23 - **Created**: 2026-10-11T21:05:18Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T22:02:58Z ## PR Description Closes #1555 ## gh-1555 W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (first shippable slice) ### What changed Migrated the legacy full-open call sites (ticket mechanism d1–d7) to windowed opens so a session past the 2 GiB gh-1073 backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path. The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). Known pre-existing, reproduced on unmodified main: `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts the VM at teardown (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`) and kills whole-directory `dart test` runs that include it — run it in isolation.
Architecture diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph before [before W1] P1[Picker / resume / trajectory / child preview] --> F[repo.open full] F -->|> 2 GiB| X[SessionException tooLarge] end subgraph after [after W1] P2[Picker · /resume · name scan · child preview] --> W[repo.open windowed] T[fa trajectory view/cost/inspect] --> W W --> H[ensureWholeLedgerResident
loadAllOlder: bounded blocks, one splice] W --> N[resolveSessionName
paged name lookup] TL[fa trajectory tail] --> W end ```

# Rework: fix CRAP ratchet failure on the `guards` leg (CI red head 973b2236)

## Issues/Notes

- **Root cause (fetched the failed job log via `gh run view 38175442643 --log-failed`):** the `CRAP + duplication` (guards) job failed at the `crap4dart analyze` CRAP ratchet step — `Max CRAP: 14.00 — FAIL (threshold: 12.00)`. The aggregate `Quality gate` check failed only as a consequence (`Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (guards)`); every other leg was green.
- Both offenders are methods **introduced by this PR** (the ratchet is whole-repo, threshold pinned at 12.0 in `crap4dart.yaml`; at 100% coverage CRAP equals cyclomatic complexity, so CC ≤ 12 is the hard rule):
  - `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder` — CC 14, 97.2% coverage → CRAP 14.00
  - `resolveTrajectorySession` (trajectory_tui.dart) — CC 13, 100% coverage → CRAP 13.00
- No open PR review threads (0 at rework start), no merge conflicts.

## Approach

Followed the repo's established ratchet pattern (same one the config comment documents for the CC-12 trio: "split into cohesive sub-dispatchers"). Pure behavior-preserving extractions — no logic changed:

1. **`WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder`** split into three cohesive members:
   - `_scanFileHeadStrips(top, maxBytes)` — the bounded forward-scan loop, returning `(records, starts, ends)`; CC 8.
   - `_isScanSkippable(entry, top)` — the three skip classes (header line, at/above window top, already-indexed straddler); CC 3.
   - `_spliceOlderAbove(records, starts, ends)` — the single-prepend splice + re-index; CC 2.
   - `loadAllOlder` keeps only the guard and orchestration; CC 14 → 4.
2. **`resolveTrajectorySession`** — the two name-match loops (foreign-repo windowed scan + `JsonlSessionRepo.sessionNameQuick`) extracted into `_openTrajectoryByName(repo, sessions, wanted)`; resolver CC 13 → 6, helper CC 8.
3. Added the `session_storage.dart` import to `trajectory_tui.dart` for the `SessionMetadata` type argument (was transitively invisible).

TDD note: the failing "test" here is the metric gate itself. RED was reproduced locally before touching code — ran `test/session/session_tree_test.dart` + `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart` + `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` under `--coverage`, formatted lcov, and re-ran `crap4dart analyze`, reproducing the CI rows exactly (14.00 / 13.00). After the extraction the same measurement shows every touched method ≤ 8 (GREEN). The pre-existing tests already cover the extracted methods at 95–100%, and the refactor is a pure extraction, so no test behavior changes.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart` — `loadAllOlder` split into `_scanFileHeadStrips` / `_isScanSkippable` / `_spliceOlderAbove` (commented as the CRAP-ratchet-motivated split).
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — name-match arm of `resolveTrajectorySession` extracted into `_openTrajectoryByName`; added `session_storage.dart` import.

- `dart test test/session test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` — **364 tests passed**.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1558 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1558 - **Title**: gh-1555 [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1555` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 11 - **Additions**: +586 - **Deletions**: -23 - **Created**: 2026-10-11T21:05:18Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T22:02:58Z ## PR Description Closes #1555 ## gh-1555 W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (first shippable slice) ### What changed Migrated the legacy full-open call sites (ticket mechanism d1–d7) to windowed opens so a session past the 2 GiB gh-1073 backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path. The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). Known pre-existing, reproduced on unmodified main: `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts the VM at teardown (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`) and kills whole-directory `dart test` runs that include it — run it in isolation.
Architecture diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph before [before W1] P1[Picker / resume / trajectory / child preview] --> F[repo.open full] F -->|> 2 GiB| X[SessionException tooLarge] end subgraph after [after W1] P2[Picker · /resume · name scan · child preview] --> W[repo.open windowed] T[fa trajectory view/cost/inspect] --> W W --> H[ensureWholeLedgerResident
loadAllOlder: bounded blocks, one splice] W --> N[resolveSessionName
paged name lookup] TL[fa trajectory tail] --> W end ```

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1558 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1558 - **Title**: gh-1555 [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1555` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 11 - **Additions**: +586 - **Deletions**: -23 - **Created**: 2026-10-11T21:05:18Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T22:02:58Z ## PR Description Closes #1555 ## gh-1555 W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (first shippable slice) ### What changed Migrated the legacy full-open call sites (ticket mechanism d1–d7) to windowed opens so a session past the 2 GiB gh-1073 backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path. The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). Known pre-existing, reproduced on unmodified main: `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts the VM at teardown (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`) and kills whole-directory `dart test` runs that include it — run it in isolation.
Architecture diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph before [before W1] P1[Picker / resume / trajectory / child preview] --> F[repo.open full] F -->|> 2 GiB| X[SessionException tooLarge] end subgraph after [after W1] P2[Picker · /resume · name scan · child preview] --> W[repo.open windowed] T[fa trajectory view/cost/inspect] --> W W --> H[ensureWholeLedgerResident
loadAllOlder: bounded blocks, one splice] W --> N[resolveSessionName
paged name lookup] TL[fa trajectory tail] --> W end ```

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1558 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1558 - **Title**: gh-1555 [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1555` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 11 - **Additions**: +586 - **Deletions**: -23 - **Created**: 2026-10-11T21:05:18Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T22:02:58Z ## PR Description Closes #1555 ## gh-1555 W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (first shippable slice) ### What changed Migrated the legacy full-open call sites (ticket mechanism d1–d7) to windowed opens so a session past the 2 GiB gh-1073 backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path. The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). Known pre-existing, reproduced on unmodified main: `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts the VM at teardown (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`) and kills whole-directory `dart test` runs that include it — run it in isolation.
Architecture diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph before [before W1] P1[Picker / resume / trajectory / child preview] --> F[repo.open full] F -->|> 2 GiB| X[SessionException tooLarge] end subgraph after [after W1] P2[Picker · /resume · name scan · child preview] --> W[repo.open windowed] T[fa trajectory view/cost/inspect] --> W W --> H[ensureWholeLedgerResident
loadAllOlder: bounded blocks, one splice] W --> N[resolveSessionName
paged name lookup] TL[fa trajectory tail] --> W end ```

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1558 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1558 - **Title**: gh-1555 [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1555` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 11 - **Additions**: +586 - **Deletions**: -23 - **Created**: 2026-10-11T21:05:18Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T22:02:58Z ## PR Description Closes #1555 ## gh-1555 W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (first shippable slice) ### What changed Migrated the legacy full-open call sites (ticket mechanism d1–d7) to windowed opens so a session past the 2 GiB gh-1073 backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path. The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). Known pre-existing, reproduced on unmodified main: `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts the VM at teardown (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`) and kills whole-directory `dart test` runs that include it — run it in isolation.

loadAllOlder: bounded blocks, one splice] W --> N[resolveSessionName
paged name lookup] TL[fa trajectory tail] --> W end ```

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1558 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1558 - **Title**: gh-1555 [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1555` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 11 - **Additions**: +586 - **Deletions**: -23 - **Created**: 2026-10-11T21:05:18Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T22:02:58Z ## PR Description Closes #1555 ## gh-1555 W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (first shippable slice) ### What changed Migrated the legacy full-open call sites (ticket mechanism d1–d7) to windowed opens so a session past the 2 GiB gh-1073 backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path. The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). Known pre-existing, reproduced on unmodified main: `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts the VM at teardown (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`) and kills whole-directory `dart test` runs that include it — run it in isolation.

loadAllOlder: bounded blocks, one splice] W --> N[resolveSessionName
paged name lookup] TL[fa trajectory tail] --> W end ```

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1558 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1558 - **Title**: gh-1555 [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1555` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 11 - **Additions**: +586 - **Deletions**: -23 - **Created**: 2026-10-11T21:05:18Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T22:02:58Z ## PR Description Closes #1555 ## gh-1555 W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (first shippable slice) ### What changed Migrated the legacy full-open call sites (ticket mechanism d1–d7) to windowed opens so a session past the 2 GiB gh-1073 backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path. The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). Known pre-existing, reproduced on unmodified main: `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts the VM at teardown (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`) and kills whole-directory `dart test` runs that include it — run it in isolation.
Architecture diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph before [before W1] P1[Picker / resume / trajectory / child preview] --> F[repo.open full] F -->|> 2 GiB| X[SessionException tooLarge] end subgraph after [after W1] P2[Picker · /resume · name scan · child preview] --> W[repo.open windowed] T[fa trajectory view/cost/inspect] --> W W --> H[ensureWholeLedgerResident
loadAllOlder: bounded blocks, one splice] W --> N[resolveSessionName
paged name lookup] TL[fa trajectory tail] --> W end ```

Followed the repo's established ratchet pattern (same one the config comment documents for the CC-12 trio: "split into cohesive sub-dispatchers"). Pure behavior-preserving extractions — no logic changed:

The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. # Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1558 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1558 - **Title**: gh-1555 [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1555` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 11 - **Additions**: +586 - **Deletions**: -23 - **Created**: 2026-10-11T21:05:18Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T22:02:58Z ## PR Description Closes #1555 ## gh-1555 W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (first shippable slice) ### What changed Migrated the legacy full-open call sites (ticket mechanism d1–d7) to windowed opens so a session past the 2 GiB gh-1073 backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path. The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). Known pre-existing, reproduced on unmodified main: `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts the VM at teardown (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`) and kills whole-directory `dart test` runs that include it — run it in isolation.
Architecture diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph before [before W1] P1[Picker / resume / trajectory / child preview] --> F[repo.open full] F -->|> 2 GiB| X[SessionException tooLarge] end subgraph after [after W1] P2[Picker · /resume · name scan · child preview] --> W[repo.open windowed] T[fa trajectory view/cost/inspect] --> W W --> H[ensureWholeLedgerResident
loadAllOlder: bounded blocks, one splice] W --> N[resolveSessionName
paged name lookup] TL[fa trajectory tail] --> W end ```

# Rework: fix CRAP ratchet failure on the `guards` leg (CI red head 973b2236)

- **Root cause (fetched the failed job log via `gh run view 38175442643 --log-failed`):** the `CRAP + duplication` (guards) job failed at the `crap4dart analyze` CRAP ratchet step — `Max CRAP: 14.00 — FAIL (threshold: 12.00)`. The aggregate `Quality gate` check failed only as a consequence (`Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (guards)`); every other leg was green.
- Both offenders are methods **introduced by this PR** (the ratchet is whole-repo, threshold pinned at 12.0 in `crap4dart.yaml`; at 100% coverage CRAP equals cyclomatic complexity, so CC ≤ 12 is the hard rule):
  - `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder` — CC 14, 97.2% coverage → CRAP 14.00
  - `resolveTrajectorySession` (trajectory_tui.dart) — CC 13, 100% coverage → CRAP 13.00
- No open PR review threads (0 at rework start), no merge conflicts.

## Approach

Followed the repo's established ratchet pattern (same one the config comment documents for the CC-12 trio: "split into cohesive sub-dispatchers"). Pure behavior-preserving extractions — no logic changed:

1. **`WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder`** split into three cohesive members:
   - `_scanFileHeadStrips(top, maxBytes)` — the bounded forward-scan loop, returning `(records, starts, ends)`; CC 8.
   - `_isScanSkippable(entry, top)` — the three skip classes (header line, at/above window top, already-indexed straddler); CC 3.
   - `_spliceOlderAbove(records, starts, ends)` — the single-prepend splice + re-index; CC 2.
   - `loadAllOlder` keeps only the guard and orchestration; CC 14 → 4.
2. **`resolveTrajectorySession`** — the two name-match loops (foreign-repo windowed scan + `JsonlSessionRepo.sessionNameQuick`) extracted into `_openTrajectoryByName(repo, sessions, wanted)`; resolver CC 13 → 6, helper CC 8.
3. Added the `session_storage.dart` import to `trajectory_tui.dart` for the `SessionMetadata` type argument (was transitively invisible).

After the extraction the same measurement shows every touched method ≤ 8 (GREEN). The pre-existing tests already cover the extracted methods at 95–100%, and the refactor is a pure extraction, so no test behavior changes.

- `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart` — `loadAllOlder` split into `_scanFileHeadStrips` / `_isScanSkippable` / `_spliceOlderAbove` (commented as the CRAP-ratchet-motivated split).

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1558 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1558 - **Title**: gh-1555 [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1555` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 11 - **Additions**: +586 - **Deletions**: -23 - **Created**: 2026-10-11T21:05:18Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T22:02:58Z ## PR Description Closes #1555 ## gh-1555 W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (first shippable slice) ### What changed Migrated the legacy full-open call sites (ticket mechanism d1–d7) to windowed opens so a session past the 2 GiB gh-1073 backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path. The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). Known pre-existing, reproduced on unmodified main: `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts the VM at teardown (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`) and kills whole-directory `dart test` runs that include it — run it in isolation.
Architecture diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph before [before W1] P1[Picker / resume / trajectory / child preview] --> F[repo.open full] F -->|> 2 GiB| X[SessionException tooLarge] end subgraph after [after W1] P2[Picker · /resume · name scan · child preview] --> W[repo.open windowed] T[fa trajectory view/cost/inspect] --> W W --> H[ensureWholeLedgerResident
loadAllOlder: bounded blocks, one splice] W --> N[resolveSessionName
paged name lookup] TL[fa trajectory tail] --> W end ```

The aggregate `Quality gate` check failed only as a consequence (`Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (guards)`); every other leg was green.
- Both offenders are methods **introduced by this PR** (the ratchet is whole-repo, threshold pinned at 12.0 in `crap4dart.yaml`; at 100% coverage CRAP equals cyclomatic complexity, so CC ≤ 12 is the hard rule):
  - `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder` — CC 14, 97.2% coverage → CRAP 14.00
  - `resolveTrajectorySession` (trajectory_tui.dart) — CC 13, 100% coverage → CRAP 13.00
- No open PR review threads (0 at rework start), no merge conflicts.

## Approach

Followed the repo's established ratchet pattern (same one the config comment documents for the CC-12 trio: "split into cohesive sub-dispatchers"). Pure behavior-preserving extractions — no logic changed:

1. **`WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder`** split into three cohesive members:
   - `_scanFileHeadStrips(top, maxBytes)` — the bounded forward-scan loop, returning `(records, starts, ends)`; CC 8.
   - `_isScanSkippable(entry, top)` — the three skip classes (header line, at/above window top, already-indexed straddler); CC 3.
   - `_spliceOlderAbove(records, starts, ends)` — the single-prepend splice + re-index; CC 2.
   - `loadAllOlder` keeps only the guard and orchestration; CC 14 → 4.
2. **`resolveTrajectorySession`** — the two name-match loops (foreign-repo windowed scan + `JsonlSessionRepo.sessionNameQuick`) extracted into `_openTrajectoryByName(repo, sessions, wanted)`; resolver CC 13 → 6, helper CC 8.

After the extraction the same measurement shows every touched method ≤ 8 (GREEN). The pre-existing tests already cover the extracted methods at 95–100%, and the refactor is a pure extraction, so no test behavior changes.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart` — `loadAllOlder` split into `_scanFileHeadStrips` / `_isScanSkippable` / `_spliceOlderAbove` (commented as the CRAP-ratchet-motivated split).
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — name-match arm of `resolveTrajectorySession` extracted into `_openTrajectoryByName`; added `session_storage.dart` import.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1558 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1558 - **Title**: gh-1555 [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1555` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 11 - **Additions**: +586 - **Deletions**: -23 - **Created**: 2026-10-11T21:05:18Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T22:02:58Z ## PR Description Closes #1555 ## gh-1555 W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (first shippable slice) ### What changed Migrated the legacy full-open call sites (ticket mechanism d1–d7) to windowed opens so a session past the 2 GiB gh-1073 backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path. The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). Known pre-existing, reproduced on unmodified main: `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts the VM at teardown (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`) and kills whole-directory `dart test` runs that include it — run it in isolation.
Architecture diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph before [before W1] P1[Picker / resume / trajectory / child preview] --> F[repo.open full] F -->|> 2 GiB| X[SessionException tooLarge] end subgraph after [after W1] P2[Picker · /resume · name scan · child preview] --> W[repo.open windowed] T[fa trajectory view/cost/inspect] --> W W --> H[ensureWholeLedgerResident
loadAllOlder: bounded blocks, one splice] W --> N[resolveSessionName
paged name lookup] TL[fa trajectory tail] --> W end ```

Followed the repo's established ratchet pattern (same one the config comment documents for the CC-12 trio: "split into cohesive sub-dispatchers"). Pure behavior-preserving extractions — no logic changed:

1. **`WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder`** split into three cohesive members:

One thing: in `_scanFileHeadStrips`, the "end" of the last entry in a chunk is computed as `entry.offset + entry.bytes + 1`. But if the chunk's last entry is exactly at the boundary of the top window, its "end" would be `offset + bytes + 1`, which is the actual line end — fine. However, a subtle issue: if the scan entry straddles `top` (offset < top but offset+bytes+1 > top)... readForward with maxBytes stopping mid-record: how does readForward handle partial records? Need to check SessionChunkReader.readForward. If a record is split across chunk boundaries, does the entry's bytes reflect the full record? Let me read the reader.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1558 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1558 - **Title**: gh-1555 [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1555` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 11 - **Additions**: +586 - **Deletions**: -23 - **Created**: 2026-10-11T21:05:18Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T22:02:58Z ## PR Description Closes #1555 ## gh-1555 W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (first shippable slice) ### What changed Migrated the legacy full-open call sites (ticket mechanism d1–d7) to windowed opens so a session past the 2 GiB gh-1073 backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path. The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). Known pre-existing, reproduced on unmodified main: `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts the VM at teardown (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`) and kills whole-directory `dart test` runs that include it — run it in isolation.

loadAllOlder: bounded blocks, one splice] W --> N[resolveSessionName
paged name lookup] TL[fa trajectory tail] --> W end ```

## Approach

Followed the repo's established ratchet pattern (same one the config comment documents for the CC-12 trio: "split into cohesive sub-dispatchers"). Pure behavior-preserving extractions — no logic changed:

1. **`WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder`** split into three cohesive members:

   - `_spliceOlderAbove(records, starts, ends)` — the single-prepend splice + re-index; CC 2.

2. **`resolveTrajectorySession`** — the two name-match loops (foreign-repo windowed scan + `JsonlSessionRepo.sessionNameQuick`) extracted into `_openTrajectoryByName(repo, sessions, wanted)`; resolver CC 13 → 6, helper CC 8.

# Rework: fix CRAP ratchet failure on the `guards` leg (CI red head 973b2236)

## Issues/Notes

- **Root cause (fetched the failed job log via `gh run view 38175442643 --log-failed`):** the `CRAP + duplication` (guards) job failed at the `crap4dart analyze` CRAP ratchet step — `Max CRAP: 14.00 — FAIL (threshold: 12.00)`. The aggregate `Quality gate` check failed only as a consequence (`Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (guards)`); every other leg was green.
- Both offenders are methods **introduced by this PR** (the ratchet is whole-repo, threshold pinned at 12.0 in `crap4dart.yaml`; at 100% coverage CRAP equals cyclomatic complexity, so CC ≤ 12 is the hard rule):
  - `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder` — CC 14, 97.2% coverage → CRAP 14.00
  - `resolveTrajectorySession` (trajectory_tui.dart) — CC 13, 100% coverage → CRAP 13.00
- No open PR review threads (0 at rework start), no merge conflicts.

## Approach

Followed the repo's established ratchet pattern (same one the config comment documents for the CC-12 trio: "split into cohesive sub-dispatchers"). Pure behavior-preserving extractions — no logic changed:

1. **`WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder`** split into three cohesive members:
   - `_scanFileHeadStrips(top, maxBytes)` — the bounded forward-scan loop, returning `(records, starts, ends)`; CC 8.
   - `_isScanSkippable(entry, top)` — the three skip classes (header line, at/above window top, already-indexed straddler); CC 3.
   - `_spliceOlderAbove(records, starts, ends)` — the single-prepend splice + re-index; CC 2.
   - `loadAllOlder` keeps only the guard and orchestration; CC 14 → 4.
2. **`resolveTrajectorySession`** — the two name-match loops (foreign-repo windowed scan + `JsonlSessionRepo.sessionNameQuick`) extracted into `_openTrajectoryByName(repo, sessions, wanted)`; resolver CC 13 → 6, helper CC 8.
3. Added the `session_storage.dart` import to `trajectory_tui.dart` for the `SessionMetadata` type argument (was transitively invisible).

TDD note: the failing "test" here is the metric gate itself. RED was reproduced locally before touching code — ran `test/session/session_tree_test.dart` + `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart` + `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` under `--coverage`, formatted lcov, and re-ran `crap4dart analyze`, reproducing the CI rows exactly (14.00 / 13.00). After the extraction the same measurement shows every touched method ≤ 8 (GREEN). The pre-existing tests already cover the extracted methods at 95–100%, and the refactor is a pure extraction, so no test behavior changes.

- `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart` — `loadAllOlder` split into `_scanFileHeadStrips` / `_isScanSkippable` / `_spliceOlderAbove` (commented as the CRAP-ratchet-motivated split).

2. Each poll re-opens a **fresh windowed** session and calls `getBranch()` — which returns only the ~200-record resident tail window (the rework summary itself notes "200 resident at open").
3. `fresh.length` (~200) `<= _seen` (N) → `tail()` returns `const []` on **every poll, forever**. No error, no exit code change — the command just stops emitting.

This breaks `fa trajectory tail` not only for the incident-class giant sessions but for **any session with more than ~200 records**, which is exactly the population this PR targets. CI stays green because no test exercises the headless tail against a >window session (the `/trajectory tail` test in `trajectory_cli_test.dart` rides the live-session path in `trajectory_commands.dart`, which is a different code path and unaffected).

**Fix options** (either works):

- Poll the *original* `session` object instead of re-opening: after `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` its window covers the whole ledger, and its live-tail ingest (`_ingestAtTail`, `windowed_session_storage.dart:736`) picks up the appended suffix on each `getBranch()`, so the branch list genuinely grows past `_seen`.
- Or skip `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` for the `tail` verb entirely (the tailer never needs the head) — cheaper startup, though the initial print then covers only the resident window instead of the old full-branch parity; if that parity matters, pair it with option 1.

A regression test should seed >window records (e.g. 300), tail headlessly, append, and assert the new record renders — see `comment4` below.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `loadAllOlder` reproduces the heap exhaustion the gh-1073 backstop was built to prevent — with no size guard**

The 2 GiB full-open refusal exists because materializing a giant ledger exhausts the heap. `loadAllOlder()` reaches the same exhaustion through the windowed door: every record above the window is parsed and retained in `_entries` **plus** three indexes (`_byId`, `_offsetById`, `_labelsById`) — for a 2.6 GiB incident-shape ledger that is very likely OOM, reached only after a multi-minute whole-file scan, where the old code failed fast with a clear `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` message pointing at `fa session repair`.

`ensureWholeLedgerResident()` (called unconditionally from `bin/fah_trajectory.dart:40` for `view`/`cost`/`inspect`) therefore degrades "clean refusal with remediation guidance" into "long hang, then probable VM crash" for exactly the sessions this ticket is about. These surfaces genuinely need the whole ledger today, so this is not a blocker — but until AC3a streaming lands, please add a cheap pre-check (`await _reader.stat()` size vs. a bound, e.g. the same 2 GiB) that throws the same `tooLarge` `SessionException` with the repair hint before the scan starts. That keeps the honest degradation contract (F3 NEG) for the truly-giant case while the chunked scan fixes the merely-large one.

Two smaller notes on the same method:

- If the scan loop breaks early on `chunk.isEmpty` (file truncated below `top` mid-scan), `_hasOlder` is still set to `false` and the window claims full residency over a range that was never read. It follows the `_readOlderBlock` "empty read ends the walk" convention, so consistent — but worth a comment that an early empty read here means *truncation*, not *clean EOF at the head*.
- `_spliceOlderAbove` is byte-for-byte the same splice logic as the new `prepend` block in `_indexChunk` (three `insertAll` + the identical per-record index/`_appendedBelow.remove`/label-cache loop). Extract one shared `_blockPrepend(records, starts, ends)` so the next window-layout change can't update one copy and miss the other.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `loadAllOlder` reproduces the heap exhaustion the gh-1073 backstop was built to prevent — with no size guard**

The 2 GiB full-open refusal exists because materializing a giant ledger exhausts the heap. `loadAllOlder()` reaches the same exhaustion through the windowed door: every record above the window is parsed and retained in `_entries` **plus** three indexes (`_byId`, `_offsetById`, `_labelsById`) — for a 2.6 GiB incident-shape ledger that is very likely OOM, reached only after a multi-minute whole-file scan, where the old code failed fast with a clear `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` message pointing at `fa session repair`.

Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. dmtools jira_search_by_jql JQL"] SOURCE -->|Confluence| C["dmtools confluence_get_page_by_url URL
dmtools confluence_search QUERY"] SOURCE -->|ADO| A["dmtools ado_get_work_item ID
dmtools ado_search_work_items QUERY"] SOURCE -->|GitHub| G["dmtools github_get_issue REPO NUM
dmtools github_search_code QUERY"] J --> PARSE["Parse JSON → use in response"] C --> PARSE A --> PARSE G --> PARSE subgraph RULES["⚠️ Rules"] R1["Check input/ first — avoid redundant fetches"] R2["Handle errors gracefully — continue with available info"] R3["Cite sources — mention where data came from"] end PARSE --> RULES NOTE["Examples:
dmtools jira_get_ticket PROJ-456 [jira-ticket]
dmtools confluence_search 'parser spec'
dmtools confluence_get_page_by_url URL"] -.-> NEED ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph USE["Use dmtools skill"] U1["Jira, Figma, Confluence, Teams, etc."] U2["Credentials preconfigured via environment variables"] end subgraph SAFETY["CLI command safety"] S1["One simple executable command at a time"] S2["DMTools rejects shell metacharacters"] end subgraph FORBIDDEN["NEVER USE"] F1["Pipes: |"] F2["Redirection: > < 2>/dev/null"] F3["Chaining: ; && ||"] F4["Substitution: backticks, $(), ${...}"] end subgraph EXAMPLES["Instead"] E1["find ... | head -20"] --> E1a["run: find ..."] E2["cmd1 && cmd2"] --> E2a["run: cmd1"] --> E2b["then: cmd2"] E3["Complex logic"] --> E3a["Write script file, run script as single command"] end subgraph CWD["Working directory discipline (persistent shell!)"] C1["Your Bash shell is ONE persistent session for the whole task — a cd in one command carries over to every later command, including Write/Edit"] C2["cd dependencies/<repo> to explore a dependency's source? You are now inside it for every subsequent command until you cd out"] C3["Forgetting to cd back before writing outputs/* silently writes to dependencies/<repo>/outputs/* instead of the job's own outputs/ — the write itself succeeds, so nothing looks wrong, but the file is lost"] C4["Before ANY Write/Edit to outputs/ (response.md, pr_review.json, pr_review_comments/*.md, etc.): run pwd first and confirm you are at the job root, not inside dependencies/"] C5["If unsure or already deep in a dependency checkout: cd to the ABSOLUTE job root path shown in the very first tool result of this session before writing outputs/*"] C6["Do NOT defensively re-cd into a directory you are already in — running cd dependencies/<repo> a second time while already inside it fails with No such file or directory (it looks for a nested dependencies/<repo>/dependencies/<repo>). Run pwd first if unsure; only cd once per direction change"] C7["For one-off commands inside a dependency checkout, prefer git -C dependencies/<repo> <command> over cd dependencies/<repo> then command — the -C form targets that directory without depending on or changing the shell cwd, so there is no cd bookkeeping to get wrong"] C8["Git global flags like --no-pager go BEFORE the subcommand: git --no-pager diff ... is correct, git diff ... --no-pager errors out (git treats the trailing flag as a positional argument)"] end subgraph BGJOBS["⚠️ Long-running commands — background execution, never foreground-poll"] B1["Any command that can run longer than ~2 minutes (full test suite, coverage run, build, dependency install, dev server or watch mode) MUST be started with bash background: true — you get a job id immediately and the completion notice arrives as a message"] B2["❌ NEVER wait for a long job with foreground sleep-polling: repeated sleep-then-check loops like sleep 540 → ls coverage. A foreground sleep pins the tool-call open — owner steering and cancel cannot reach you until it ends — and burns wall-clock plus a runner slot"] B3["While a background job runs, keep working on other steps — check progress between steps with bash_job status / bash_job output <job-id> — never park the turn in a watch loop"] B4["A harness hint like background candidate: bash background: true, job board /tasks, --wait-for-jobs is an ORDER, not a suggestion — obey it and start the command in the background; working around it with foreground sleeps is a violation"] B5["Verification order: finalize ALL code edits BEFORE launching a long verification run (full suite, coverage) — verification must run against a frozen tree, otherwise the run is wasted"] B6["Files changed while a verification run is in flight? Do NOT kill it mid-flight — let it finish, treat the result as stale, then deliberately start a fresh run against the updated tree"] B7["B6 covers a job still making progress — do NOT kill it mid-flight; a job with NO progress for ~10 min (or 2× its expected duration) is HUNG — dispose of it and MOVE ON: bash_job stop <job-id>, note the disposal in the deliverable (job id, command, last output tail), finish the remaining steps and write outputs/response.md reporting the unverified part. NEVER let a hung child hold the deliverable hostage: validation CI on the pull request is the safety net"] B1 --> B2 --> B3 --> B4 --> B5 --> B6 --> B7 end USE --> SAFETY SAFETY --> FORBIDDEN SAFETY --> EXAMPLES SAFETY --> CWD CWD --> BGJOBS ``` # Review verdict rules — machine protocol (binding) The review↔rework loop is a machine, not a conversation: your `recommendation` in `outputs/pr_review.json` is parsed mechanically and drives issue labels, rework runs and CI (each wasted round costs 15–20 CI minutes — gh-71). These rules govern the verdict; every other instruction (severity definitions, output files, thread etiquette) is unchanged. ## Verdict mapping Classify findings exactly as instructed: - 🚨 **BLOCKING** — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss. - ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR works as shipped. - 💡 **SUGGESTION** — style, wording, import order, dartdoc refs, polish. Then map to the verdict: | Findings | `recommendation` | |---|---| | Any 🚨 BLOCKING (correctness/bug) | `REQUEST_CHANGES` — or `BLOCK` for security / data loss | | No 🚨 BLOCKING — only ⚠️ / 💡 remain | `APPROVE` | `APPROVE` with remaining ⚠️/💡 findings is the expected terminal state (`allowApproveWithSuggestions: true`): post every remaining finding as before (inline threads + general comment) — they do **not** block the merge and must **not** trigger another rework round. ## Anti-patterns (observed live, gh-71) - ❌ Returning `REQUEST_CHANGES` because a re-review surfaced new suggestion-level nits (docs wording, import style, dartdoc refs). A cycle with only suggestion-level findings **must** converge to `APPROVE`. - ❌ `REQUEST_CHANGES` while `issueCounts.blocking` is `0` — the machine treats that as an approval and skips the rework round. Keep `issueCounts` accurate: it is the machine's source of truth, not prose. The machine also cross-checks the counter against your inline comments (a `severity: "BLOCKING"` entry or a 🚨 marker in the referenced comment file) before honoring a blocking-0 approval — if any finding is truly blocking, set `recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES` with `blocking: 1`+. - ❌ Verdict-by-prose: never phrase the verdict only in the summary text. The `recommendation` field of `outputs/pr_review.json` is the verdict. - ❌ Re-opening a thread that the rework demonstrably fixed in this diff — add its id to `resolvedThreadIds` instead. ## Label guard rails — the chore:pin lane (live: fa pr-1104, 2026-09-30) `chore:pin` is a trusted, **non-exclusive** factory fast-lane: several PRs may carry it at the same time (a release bump `chore/release-vX.Y.Z` AND a factory pin `chore/factory-pin-*` are both legitimate holders — they ride the lane independently). Reviews must therefore: - ❌ **NEVER remove `chore:pin` from any PR** — not as a "one pin" dedup, not as a side-effect of closing a related PR as superseded. Removing it from the release bump stranded the v1.0.494 tag behind the guest queue for an hour (fa pr-1104, unlabeled 13:31:08Z while pr-1105 was closed). - ✅ When a PR is superseded (e.g. a workflow change already shipped via another PR), close **only that PR** and leave every label on every other PR untouched. Label restoration is a keeper action, not yours. - ✅ If you believe two `chore:pin` holders conflict, SAY SO in the review comment and keep both labels — the owner resolves the lane, the machine only merges.
